nativeRvaLock.note: The three implemented rows submit members of the enemy's own state machines and AI (ES_HibernateWakeUp.ActivateState, EnemyBehaviour.ChangeState, EnemyAI.NavmeshAgentGoal). They are reached through the interop assembly by type and member name, so no test locks these RVAs; this file is the build-specific record of the members the actions write and the readback each commit is confirmed with.

hookMembers.name: ActivateState
hookMembers.rawDeclaration: void ActivateState(Vector3 direction, float distance, float delay, bool isPropagatedWakeup)
observations: 3 callers, all hibernation detection paths of the same enemy: EB_Hibernating.UpdateDetection at 0x166CC65 and EB_Hibernating.OnNoiseDetected at 0x166C2BB and 0x166C124. It is what the game itself runs when something wakes an enemy.

the body loads the enemy transform's forward (Component.get_transform 0x17FCF32, Transform.get_forward 0x17FCF50), tests Vector3.Dot (0x17FCFA2) to decide whether the wake turns, and picks an animation index with EnemyLocomotion.GetRandomAnimIndex (0x17FD03C). Every one of those is a store into the state's own fields: m_isTurn, m_animationIndex, m_delayTime, m_isPropagatedWakeup

the state's four fields are declared as a replicated payload: pES_HibernateWakeup { byte animationIndex; bool isTurn; float delay; bool isPropagatedWakeup } is an Explicit-layout struct, and ES_HibernateWakeUp.RecieveStateData(pES_HibernateWakeup) is the client-side applier

the wake ends through ES_HibernateWakeUp.Exit, which calls EnemyBehaviour.ChangeState at 0x17FDAC3: leaving hibernation is a behaviour-machine transition, so the awakened fact and this action agree on what waking is

conclusions.detail: The row declares a `slot` output of type handle with handleKind `lease` and lifetime `entity_life`, and its recipient contract names that handle as the action's handle output. The runtime's handle pool is the kernel's own: RuntimeKernel.CreateHandle is private and only the control steps' timers use it, while RuntimeModuleHandle exposes Publish, CancelScope and Dispose and nothing else. A provider can therefore neither mint the handle its row declares nor register the native target slot that handle would name, and a handle this assembly invented would be a second handle namespace the kernel's CheckHandle does not own. What the action needs is the framework feature the runtime's own ABI plan already schedules (provider-minted handles plus a handle-to-native-object table and a cancel hook); until it exists this row cannot be implemented without faking it.
conclusions.nativeWritePointFound: AgentAI.set_Target(AgentTarget) / AgentAI.SetTarget(Agent) / EnemyAI.SetTarget(Agent) / AgentAI.SetDetectedAgent(Agent, AgentTargetDetectionType) are public and present, so the write itself is reachable when the handle feature exists

conclusions.detail: The row's only recipient input is `slots`, a many handle of kind `lease` and lifetime `entity_life`: there is nothing to clear without a handle minted by target_set's row, which cannot be minted at all. The row is therefore not declared rather than declared and unusable.

The row's recipient input is `machines`, a many handle of kind `lease` and lifetime `entity_life`, so it has the same missing prerequisite as target_clear. It also carries a second, independent shape problem: the native machine has two state enums. `EB_States` (29 members) is the behaviour machine EnemyBehaviour.ChangeState writes, and `ES_StateEnum` (34 members) is the locomotion machine EnemyLocomotion.ChangeState writes. The catalog's `ai_state` set has 12 members, and its members cannot be mapped one-to-one: `alerted` and `pursuing` both name EB_States.InCombat (5), `sleeping`/`waking`/`hibernating` name three different native members across the two machines, `disabled` has no native member at all, and `waking` is SquidBoss_Intro (13), which exists only on the boss. A state_request that accepted those members would silently fold several of them into one native state or invent a transition, which the row's own note forbids.

unverified.topic: client-side replication of the three writes
unverified.note: The static evidence shows the game's own replication paths for the behaviour state (EnemySync.IncomingState), the hibernation states (pES_HibernateState / pES_HibernateWakeup payloads with RecieveStateData appliers) and the path data (pEnemyPathData). Whether a host-side write of these members at an arbitrary moment — rather than inside the game's own update — produces the same packets on the same frame is not observable offline and needs host plus one client in game.

unverified.topic: area_field provider for move_to's area port
unverified.note: The area port is refused here because no native navigation member consumes a region. If the map package's area_field provider later gives a region a meaning the navigation contract carries, the refusal can be lifted; the port stays in the row until then so the catalog and the binding do not drift.
